kf: **Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE)** is chronic cutaneous lupus: scaly red plaques that heal with **scarring, atrophy and pigment change**.
Face, ears (conchal bowl), scalp (scarring alopecia); photosensitive; follicular plugging ('carpet-tack' scale).
About 5–10% progress to systemic lupus; check FBC, ANA, ENA, urine.
Strict photoprotection, **stop smoking**, potent topical steroid; **hydroxychloroquine** via dermatology.

sub: Women 20–40; more common and more scarring in people of African descent.

myths: **"It's just eczema on the face"**: scarring, follicular plugs and ear involvement point to DLE.
patho_lead: DLE is an **interface attack** on basal keratinocytes and hair follicles, triggered by UV.

mech.t: UV causes keratinocyte apoptosis and exposure of nuclear antigens.
Plasmacytoid dendritic cells produce type I interferon, recruiting cytotoxic T cells.
T cells attack the basal layer and follicular epithelium.
Follicles are destroyed, leaving permanent scarring alopecia and atrophy.

histo: Interface dermatitis, follicular plugging, thickened basement membrane, perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytes, dermal mucin; DIF: lupus band.

sub: Marked hyper- and depigmentation; high scarring risk.

comp: Scarring alopecia, disfigurement, SCC in scars, progression to SLE.
